notes:
Summary: Mid-market SaaS team building an embedded support assistant + internal reranking pipeline. Currently running a Hosted POC to validate parity with their OpenAI-based stack before committing to Dedicated.

Key technical details / snippets from calls:
- "OpenAI parity" is the sentiment used by the product lead — they expect near-identical output for NPS-critical summarization flows.
- POC setup: migrated ~120 prompt templates + 40 evaluation queries. Using existing user embeddings pipeline (FAISS) — testing Redwood embeddings for semantic search.
- Observed: 8% BLEU-like drop for summarization prompts; reranking reorder differences on ~12% of top-5 queries. Latency was within targets on Hosted when using auto-batching.
- Cost sensitivity: current monthly spend on OpenAI ~ $9k; aiming to reduce unit token costs by 30-40% with Dedicated and caching.
- Security: require SSO/SAML, SOC2, KMS for key custody, and contractual data residency (EU) for EU traffic.

AE notes / shorthand:
- "SE working on prompt shim to reduce regressions; experiment with temperature/penalty + instruction templates"
- "Legal asked for residency clause sample — shared Drive link (see linked_drive_docs)"
- "Procurement: needs 2 approvals; CFO will sign if ARR estimate < $100k/year, else requires VP approval"

Quoted from product lead: "We need the answers to 'does it behave exactly the same?' before we talk committed spend.'"
migration_plan: Phase 1: Hosted POC to validate prompt parity and embeddings replacements; Phase 2: Optimize batching, caching, and cost model; Phase 3: Dedicated sizing + VPC setup (EU region) and contract; Phase 4: Cutover with dual-write comparison and rollback policy. Typical duration 8-12 weeks.
risk_assessment: Medium — technical risk centered on prompt parity/regressions and EU residency legal approval. Cost risk manageable if 30%+ token savings realized on Dedicated.
